text:
SEATTLE — South Korea's notoriously competitive college entrance exam has long fascinated international audiences for its grueling questions and the extraordinary measures the country takes to ensure a smooth testing environment. This year, however, the exam is drawing global attention for an entirely different reason: artificial intelligence (AI).
As hundreds of thousands of students sit for the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), better known as Suneung, Thursday, people outside Korea are closely following the country's efforts to prevent AI-assisted cheating.
International media outlets, including CNN, BBC and ABC News, have reported extensively in recent days on the government's rush to tighten exam security following the confession of the top scorer in Korea's certified tax accountant exam, who admitted to cheating using a miniature camera and generative AI.
The unusual security measures introduced for this year's exam, including inspections of students' glasses and clothing buttons for hidden cameras, have caught the attention of foreign readers. So has President Lee Jae Myung's proposal to consider offering cash rewards of 100 million won or more for reporting cheating.
On Instagram, users commenting on news coverage of the CSAT expressed sympathy for Korean students facing the added pressure of heightened exam security.
“Eight hours of back-to-back exam is brutal enough, and then there’s the whole cheating crackdown on top of it,” one user wrote.
“The pressure on these students must be huge,” another commented.
Others were struck by the extent to which the country adjusts its daily routines for the exam.
“The whole country pausing for one exam. That’s wild,” one user wrote, while another commented, “Wonder if there will be any cheating attempts.”
On Reddit, the Korean cheating scandal has been brought up in forums for prospective law and dental school students in the U.S., as well as those dedicated to AI and smart glasses.
“Suddenly, everyone is a proctor now,” one user wrote, referring to the proposed cash rewards for reporting cheating. “False accusation drama is going to be wild.”
Last year, much of the overseas interest in the CSAT stemmed from its exceptionally difficult English questions, which went viral as native English speakers shared their attempts at answering them on social media. This year, much of the discussion has centered on exam security.
